text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- A top ally of German Finance Minister Theo Waigel warns the Defence Ministry not to try to squeeze additional funds from the state to fund Germany's share of the four-nation Eurofighter aircraft project.
- The causes of a fire in a Luebeck church three weeks ago seem to be largely cleared up as police detain a 19-year old.

- Bonn and Paris at pains to find agreement on Maastricht II contract in Amsterdam with both Finance Minister Waigel and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel signalling that they should be able to reach a deal.
- Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) offers to fill large budget gap in the four-nation Eurofighter project.
HANDELSBLATT
- Bonn against spending any more money on job creation as European Union leaders start summit in Amsterdam.
- German banks tell Handelsblatt that a delay to the start of the planned European single currency would have unthinkable consequences.
- Government due to sell shares in state-owned Tank & Rast AG onto the open market rather than to an intermediary, bringing Bonn around 700 million marks.
- Tax increases in 1998 seem to have been finally ruled out as Finance Minister Theo Waigel announces new cuts.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bonn coalition rules out tax increases for 1998. Budget shortfall of 20 billion marks should be covered by privatisations and savings in all departments.
- Unknown arsonists set a fire at the alter of a church in Husum, the third fire in a German church in recent weeks.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl says he sees no real turn around on the jobs market in 1998.
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and industry reject ruling coalition's amended tax reform plans.
DIE WELT
- Another arson attack on a church in northern Germany as unknown assailants set fire to alter of Husum church.
- Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) attacks Defence Minister Volker Ruehe over Eurofighter financing plans.
- Almost 3,000 protesting farmers greet Chancellor Kohl with whistles and shouts as he arrives in Bad Woerishofen.
